summary: Yuichi Kajiyama worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, SOAS, and Vienna under J. Kashab, Satkari Mookerjee, John Brough, and Erich Frauwallner. He held posts at Kyoto University, Bukkyo University, and Soka University.

Yuishin Ito specialized in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Bukkyo University and Doshisha University. He held positions at Bukkyo University, including lecturer in 1961 and professor emeritus (1974–1997), and served as president of Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College in 1997.

Yujiro Motora was a scholar in philosophy and other fields. He studied at Johns Hopkins University in 1885 and held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1888–1912) and Tokyo University of Education (~1890).

Yujun Endo specialized in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held appointments at Taisho University, where he was attested as associate professor in 1991 and professor emeritus in 2014, and at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Yuka Otani is a scholar of Buddhist studies. In 2015, she was attested as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University and Hanazono University.

Yukari Kimura specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her doctoral studies under Kenyo Mitomo and was attested in 2026 as a part-time lecturer at Rissho University affiliated with the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Yukei Matsunaga worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Koyasan University, Tohoku University, and Kyushu University. He served as director at Koyasan University in 1983 and held a post at Shuchiin University around 1998.

Yuki Sasaki is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. In 2026, Sasaki was attested as a part-time lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Yukihiko Asayama worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He was attested as a professor at Hokkaido University of Education in 1986 and as an overseas research fellow at South China Normal University in 1991.
Yukihiko Matsumura is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Tohoku University (attested 2015), where he was also attested as a specialist researcher in 2026.

Yukihiro Okada works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo and under Michael Hahn. He served at Kobe Women's University Seto Junior College, and as an advisor at Minobusan University (attested 2026).
Yukihisa Yamao specialized in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Ritsumeikan University from ~1954 to 1960 and held an academic post there from ~1974 to 1999.
Yukio Hattori worked in Japanology and history and archaeology. He studied at Nagoya University and held an academic post at Japan Women's University.

Yukio Kotani is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Hanjiro Tominaga. He served at Rissho University from ~1970 to 2002, becoming professor emeritus of comparative literature.

Yukio Sakamoto studied Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo under Taiken Kimura and Daito Shimaji, earning a doctorate from Tohoku University. He held posts at Rissho University, including president in 1968, and was a professor at Toyo University (~1956–1970).
Yukio Yamanaka specializes in Indology and philosophy. He was a graduate student at Kyoto University (attested 1996) and was attested in 2015 as a DFG Research Fellow at the University of Göttingen.

Yuko Kamishima works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied at Indiana University Bloomington, Cambridge, and the University of Tokyo, and under Ekai Kawaguchi. She served as an assistant at Waseda University (2006–2016) and became professor at Ritsumeikan University in 2016.
Yuko Matsuda is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin Women's Junior College and held an affiliation with Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College, attested in 2001.

Yuko Yokochi specializes in Indology. She studied at the University of Tokyo and the University of Groningen under Minoru Hara, Katsuhiko Kamimura, and Hans T. Bakker. She held posts as associate professor and professor at Kyoto University.
Yulian Zeng works in the field of Buddhist studies. Zeng earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin, and also studied under traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
